> 207	/** Parse the MAX YAVG in a metadata=print file (single frame → one line, but MAX is robust to more). */
> 208	function readYavg(file: string): number | null {

> 214	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;

> 216	    const v = Number.parseFloat(m[1]);
> 217	    if (Number.isFinite(v)) max = max === null ? v : Math.max(max, v);
> 218	  }
> 219	  return max;
> 220	}

> 222	/** Deterministic sample instants across the cut: start / mid / end (end nudged just inside the window). */
> 223	function sampleTimes(inSec: number, outSec: number, count: number): number[] {
> 224	  const start = Math.max(0, Number.isFinite(inSec) ? inSec : 0);
> 225	  const end = Math.max(start, Number.isFinite(outSec) ? outSec : start);
> 226	  const span = end - start;
> 227	  if (span <= 0.3 || count <= 1) return [start];
> 228	  const nudge = Math.min(0.1, span * 0.05);
> 229	  const mid = start + span / 2;
> 230	  const last = Math.max(start, end - nudge);
> 231	  const all = count >= 3 ? [start, mid, last] : [start, last];
> 232	  // Dedupe near-identical instants (a tiny window can collapse mid/last onto the endpoints).
> 233	  const out: number[] = [];
> 234	  for (const t of all) if (!out.some((u) => Math.abs(u - t) < 0.02)) out.push(t);
> 235	  return out;
> 236	}

The detector runs at about 33-36ms per frame after warmup on 608×1080 resolution, with initial model and WASM loading taking roughly 300ms. Now I'm setting up a new TypeScript module that exports a face region detector function, which takes a video source and array of timestamps, then extracts frames at those times using the same 9:16 center-crop reframing pipeline that the zone segmentation already uses.

The detector spins up a headless Chromium browser (cached and reused across clips to avoid repeated startup overhead) running FaceDetector to identify faces in each frame. It normalizes the bounding boxes to canvas fractions, unions them across all timestamps to build a forbidden region map, and gracefully degrades to an empty result if anything fails. Then I'm updating the zone picker to account for these forbidden regions by calculating how much each candidate zone overlaps with them. The face detection acts as a filter to exclude overlapping zones before selecting the calmest one, so a detected face on the right side naturally pushes the card placement leftward or lower. I need to handle a few risks: tasks-vision isn't declared as a dependency and the model file needs to be vendored in the repo rather than relying on an orphan node_modules copy, and blazeface's frontal bias means it struggles with profile shots and small faces—I'll mitigate this with a lower confidence threshold around 0.35, sampling across multiple frames, and falling back gracefully when detection fails.

Low thresholds do introduce false positives from bright screen glare, but that's cosmetic since a spurious forbidden zone just shifts text placement. The bigger constraint is browser startup time—launching a fresh detector per clip would exceed my time budget, so I need to reuse a singleton across all clips. I haven't tested multi-face scenarios or occluded faces yet, and blazeface won't catch those anyway, but the fail-open logic handles it.
